newsitem.title: UK: Spain's ICO plans $500 million Eurobond - traders.
newsitem.headline: Spain's ICO plans $500 million Eurobond - traders.

text.p: Banks are bidding for the mandate for an expected Eurobond from Spain's Instituto de Credito Oficial (ICO), new issues traders said on Friday.
They said the issue from the Spanish Government Development Bank, headquartered in Madrid, was likely to be launched in early December.
Euromarket expectations for a more imminent date was premature, dealers said.
"It's all still a bit premature. No one has yet offically been mandated," a syndicate manager at a U.S. house said.
ICO is expected to launch a Eurobond of up to $500 million guaranteed by the Kingdom of Spain. It is likely to mature after five years.
Some traders said current price talk was in the region of 18 basis points over U.S. Treasury notes and said Goldman Sachs were tipped as the lead manager for the transaction.
But a Goldman Sachs syndicate official said no mandate had yet been awarded.
Initially, a $200 million two-year deal was mooted, but ICO wanted a larger more liquid transaction, traders said.
In October 1990, Goldman lead-managed a $450 million seven-year FRN for ICO.
Moody's Investors Service rates ICO, AA2, and Standard & Poor's Corp rates the borrower AA.
